found.domain: settlement-loop-hunter: cross-domain hunt for named institutional mechanisms that turn a case decision into a prospective rule (IRS PLR->Rev Proc, French rescrit->BOFiP, EU/UK BTI, SSA SSR/AR/POMS, VA GC precedent opinions, USCIS adopted decisions/Policy Manual, bank/securities regulator letters, FASB/IFRS IC/Big-4 consultation, insurer bulletins, construction RFI->ASI, Meta Oversight Board, policy clarification logs, IAM exception registers, UK Upper Tribunal->DWP ADM, ISO/ASME interpretations, legal KM, interpretation registers) and the opposite pattern (explicit non-precedent)

workflows.name: IRS private letter rulings (PLRs) -> revenue procedures / automatic-consent procedures / no-rule lists
workflows.decision_volume: Scraped IRS written-determination corpus (28,135 files, github.com/surabhitri/PLR_Classification, counted locally by filename year prefix; source type: primary-derived dataset scraped from irs.gov, secondary host): 1999: 1,407; 2000: 1,644; 2001: 1,721; 2002: 1,702; 2005: 1,407; 2008: 1,321; 2010: 1,348; 2012: 850; 2014: ~1,124; 2015: 1,043; 2018: 582; 2020: 547; 2022: 719; 2023: 693 (a separate 2023_PLRs folder holds 785). These are lower bounds for PLRs proper (corpus filtered to 'definite PLR'). An academic text in the same repo (PLR_Context_+.pdf) reports 'approximately 81,000 PLRs' after excluding mandatory/non-discretionary rulings (cumulative universe). SOURCED, secondary host of primary documents.
workflows.human_review_rate: 100% by construction: a PLR is a human legal opinion written by IRS Chief Counsel on request (primary PLR text, github.com/surabhitri/PLR_Classification/blob/main/data/raw/files_definite_plr/202301001.pdf). Share of all tax positions that go to a PLR is tiny (hundreds per year vs ~10^8 returns; the return count is recalled, not fetched).
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: PLR subject matter and the Rev. Proc. no-rule list described in PLR_Context_+.pdf, which states the IRS annually lists issues it will not rule on because they are 'factual questions'): C rule interpretation ~50%, B factual classification ~15% (partly excluded via no-rule list), G one-off transaction structure ~20%, H repeatable ambiguity ~15% (evidenced by the IRS practice, described in the same PDF, of issuing 'guidelines for requests on recurring subjects'). A/D/E/F small. Analytical estimate, not measured.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Each PLR carries the statutory disclaimer: 'This ruling is directed only to the taxpayer requesting it. Section 6110(k)(3) provides that it may not be used or cited as precedent.' (quoted from PLR 202301001, 202301003, 202301004 via crude text extraction). The individual settlement is explicitly non-prospective for anyone else.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: regulator (IRS written determination, mirrored on GitHub)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Only by the requesting taxpayer for the described transaction; others use PLRs informally as signals of IRS reasoning (publedge PRIOR-ART: 'PLRs cannot be cited by other taxpayers as authority, but they signal the IRS's reasoning').

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Conversion path: the IRS issues 'guidelines for requests on recurring subjects' (revenue procedures with checklists/representations) and an annual no-rule list; user fee 'as of February 4, 2021, is generally $38,000' (determination letter $275). The fee and the recurring-subject procedures show that recurring PLR classes are absorbed into standardised procedures rather than repeated as individual rulings.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: academic (paper excerpt stored in a GitHub research repo; underlying Rev. Proc. not fetched)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Recurring PLR subjects become revenue procedures (e.g., automatic accounting-method-change consents, automatic 9100 relief) that later taxpayers apply without a ruling. RECALLED mechanism (Rev. Proc. 2015-13 list of automatic changes; Rev. Proc. 2003-16 automatic late-rollover relief) - not verified this session; canonical source irs.gov/irb (blocked).

settlement_loop_evidence.description: PLR volume in the corpus fell from ~1,700/yr (2001-2002) to ~550-800/yr (2018-2023) while the user fee rose to $38,000: consistent with recurring classes being absorbed into published procedures and with pricing rationing individual settlements.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Trend evidence only; the causal split between fee rationing and rule absorption is not established.

workflows.economic_pain: $38,000 user fee per ruling (PLR_Context_+.pdf citing the 2021 Rev. Proc.) plus practitioner fees (not sourced). Processing time not sourced (Rev. Proc. goal recalled as ~180 days for most rulings; irs.gov blocked).
workflows.existing_solutions: IRS Office of Chief Counsel, Internal Revenue Bulletin (Rev. Ruls/Rev. Procs), Written Determinations reading room (PDF only); commercial tax research (Bloomberg Tax, Checkpoint, Tax Notes) index PLRs by code section. Settlements are captured as numbered, dated, versioned prose documents (identifier stable: PLR-YYYYWWNNN) but are not executable and, by statute, not precedential (publedge PRIOR-ART).
workflows.buyer_and_budget: No software buyer for the public mechanism (IRS is the owner). Corporate tax departments and Big-4 tax practices maintain internal 'positions' libraries; budget exists but sits in tax research/GRC tooling. Not a Sophon wedge.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: 26 USC 6110(k)(3) forbids precedential use; FOIA-driven redaction; rulings are legal opinions signed by counsel.
workflows.notes: The loop is real (recurring subjects -> revenue procedure -> later cases decided by procedure without a ruling) but slow (years), prose-only, ratified by Chief Counsel/Treasury, and volume is ~10^2-10^3 settlements per year nationally. Demonstrates that a mature institution deliberately separates 'settle this case' (non-precedential, priced at $38k) from 'make a rule' (published guidance).

workflows.name: French rescrit fiscal (LPF L80A/L80B) -> BOFiP 'rescrits de portee generale' (BOI-RES series)
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED this session (impots.gouv.fr, ccomptes.fr, economie.gouv.fr, data.economie.gouv.fr all blocked). Recalled order of magnitude: DGFiP handles on the order of 10^4 rescrit requests per year (unverified; verify at https://www.economie.gouv.fr/dgfip/rapport-dactivite). BOFiP open dataset 'bofip-vigueur' contains 9,035 BOI documents with weekly updates and includes a 'Rulings' document type (SOURCED via secondary README: github.com/danielhadjaj-law/bofip-mcp, citing data.economie.gouv.fr).
workflows.human_review_rate: 100% (a rescrit is a written administrative position on a taxpayer's stated facts). Share of taxpayer questions that become rescrits: unknown.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: legal design of the rescrit, which answers a question of law on stated facts): C ~55%, B ~15%, H ~20% (the existence of a published general-scope series implies recurring questions are generalised), G ~10%. Analytical estimate.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: BOFiP content is 'opposable to the administration' under LPF L80A/L80B; the open dataset holds only the currently-in-force version, with historical versions reachable via official BOFiP URLs (versioning exists but is not in the open data). Individual rescrits bind only the requester; those of general interest are published in BOFiP (RES series) and become opposable by all taxpayers.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: vendor/open-source README (secondary) describing DGFiP open data; legal texts not fetched (legifrance.gouv.fr, bofip.impots.gouv.fr blocked)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Published RES entries are doctrine: later cases are decided by the published position; enforcement officers cannot contradict it (L80A). Ratifier: DGFiP central services. Lag and share of rescrits published: unknown.

workflows.economic_pain: Unknown this session. 3-month response deadline and tacit-acceptance rules for certain rescrits are RECALLED (LPF L80B), not verified.
workflows.existing_solutions: DGFiP internal case handling; BOFiP as the doctrine store (weekly open-data JSON, prose content); commercial doctrine databases (Lefebvre Dalloz, Lamy). Settlements published are versioned prose with 'in force' dating; not executable.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: No software buyer for the public mechanism; corporate tax and Big-4 France maintain internal rescrit/position libraries (budget unknown).
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Only published doctrine is opposable erga omnes; unpublished rescrits are opposable only by the requester; secrecy (secret fiscal) limits sharing.
workflows.notes: Structurally the cleanest public settlement loop (case -> published, opposable, versioned doctrine) but no volumes, lags or publication rates could be verified; French Cour des comptes has reported on rescrits (ccomptes.fr blocked).

workflows.name: EU Binding Tariff Information (BTI) / UK Advance Tariff Rulings (ATaR) -> published rulings, classification regulations
workflows.decision_volume: EU BTI decisions per year: NOT SOURCED (taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu, ec.europa.eu EBTI database blocked); recalled order of magnitude 'tens of thousands per year EU-wide' (unverified). UK ATaR volumes: not published in the HMRC repos. SOURCED structural facts: HMRC's open-source case system tracks every case with daysElapsed and referredDaysElapsed for SLA reporting (github.com/hmrc/binding-tariff-classification, ReportField.scala, Case.scala).
workflows.human_review_rate: 100% of applications are decided by a classification officer (roles: classification officer, manager, read-only user; github.com/hmrc/tariff-classification-frontend). Referral to other teams occurs for REQUEST_SAMPLE or REQUEST_MORE_INFO only (ReferralReason.scala) and to expert/lab advice (EventType EXPERT_ADVICE_RECEIVED); MiscCaseType includes 'Harmonised systems', 'Nomenclature', 'Appeals', 'Other government dept'.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: the HMRC data model, where the only coded escalation reasons are missing sample / more information, and the Decision record's method fields): A missing evidence ~30% (the only formal referral reasons are evidence requests), B factual classification ~40% (what the goods are; samples, lab tests), C interpretation of GIR/HS rules ~15%, H repeatable ambiguity ~10% (same product classes recur across traders; EU resolves divergences via classification regulations), D conflict of authorities ~5% (divergent BTIs between member states). Analytical estimate anchored to the sourced code.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Each ruling is a structured settlement record: Decision(bindingCommodityCode, effectiveStartDate, effectiveEndDate, justification, goodsDescription, methodSearch, methodCommercialDenomination, methodExclusion, appeal[], cancellation, explanation, decisionPdf, letterPdf). Cases carry a governed keyword vocabulary (Keyword(name, approved: Boolean), NewKeywordRequest; keywords proposed by officers and approved by managers) and a full event log (CASE_CREATED, CASE_REFERRAL, QUEUE_CHANGE, ASSIGNMENT_CHANGE, EXPERT_ADVICE_RECEIVED, CASE_COMPLETED, APPEAL_ADDED, APPEAL_STATUS_CHANGE, EXTENDED_USE_STATUS_CHANGE). Statuses: DRAFT, NEW, OPEN, SUPPRESSED, REFERRED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUSPENDED, COMPLETED, REVOKED, ANNULLED. Appeal ladder: ADR, REVIEW, APPEAL_TIER_1, APPEAL_TIER_2, COURT_OF_APPEALS, SUPREME_COURT.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Completed rulings are pushed to the public 'Search for Advance Tariff Rulings' service (refresh on completion plus two daily jobs for newly granted and cancelled rulings; github.com/hmrc/binding-tariff-ruling-frontend) so importers, exporters, agents and officers can find rulings 'currently in effect' for similar goods. Ruling binds HMRC and the holder for 3 years (UCC Art. 33 recalled; not fetched). The 'methodSearch' field records how the officer searched prior rulings before deciding - reuse of precedent is built into the decision record.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: HMRC also runs Advance Valuation Rulings (advance-valuation-rulings, -frontend, performance tests) on the same pattern; six 'ruling' repositories are active as of May-Sep 2026.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Same structured-ruling pattern extended to customs valuation.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: EU-level generalisation: divergent BTIs across member states are escalated to the Customs Code Committee, which produces Commission classification regulations and CN Explanatory Notes binding on all authorities and traders. RECALLED mechanism; volumes (recalled: dozens of classification regulations per year) not verified; EBTI database and eur-lex blocked.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Classification regulations map named goods to CN codes; consumed by TARIC and commercial classification tools (machine-consumed at the code level; rationale remains prose).

workflows.economic_pain: Not sourced. UCC time limit for BTI decisions is 120 days (recalled). HMRC tracks elapsed and referred days per case for reporting, implying SLA pressure (sourced code).
workflows.existing_solutions: Government case systems (HMRC's is open source; EU EBTI). On the trader side, Global Trade Management suites (SAP GTS, Oracle GTM, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Global Trade, Descartes CustomsInfo, Avalara, 3CE) hold internal classification databases with rationale and approval - RECALLED vendor landscape, not fetched. Settlements are captured as versioned, dated, structured records with justification; the classification itself (commodity code) is machine-consumed, the reasoning is prose.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Trade compliance managers at importers/brokers (GTM budgets); customs authorities build in-house. For a Sophon-shaped product the risk is that classification-database features already live in GTM suites (H6).
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Ruling binds only holder and authorities for the described goods; 3-year validity; revocation when regulations/explanatory notes change; publication is mandatory (EU) with confidentiality carve-outs.
workflows.notes: The most operational public settlement loop found: structured, versioned, dated, published, searched before deciding, governed keyword vocabulary, appeal ladder, SLA clocks, and a formal escalation path to EU-wide rules. But the primary escalation reasons coded in the system are evidence requests (A), not interpretation (H), which supports H1 for the front-line workflow.

workflows.name: Social Security Administration: SSRs, Acquiescence Rulings, POMS updates
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED (ssa.gov, ecfr.gov, federalregister.gov blocked). Recalled: SSA hearing-level dispositions on the order of 4-5 x10^5 per year; Social Security Rulings issued per year in the low single digits (e.g., three SSRs in 2024: 24-1p, 24-2p, 24-3p); Acquiescence Rulings rare in recent decades. All unverified; verify at https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/rulings/rulings.html.
workflows.human_review_rate: Initial disability claims: 100% decided by DDS examiners with medical consultants; reconsideration and ALJ hearing stages are human. Shares not sourced.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: disability adjudication structure, recalled): A missing medical evidence ~35%, B factual/functional classification ~35%, C rule interpretation ~10%, E discretion/credibility ~10%, H ~5%, D ~5% (circuit splits). Analytical, unverified.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: 20 CFR 402.35(b)(1): SSRs and ARs are binding on all components of SSA; ARs (20 CFR 404.985) are issued when a circuit court holding conflicts with SSA's interpretation and apply only within that circuit; POMS is the operational manual updated via transmittals and consumed by adjudicators and DDS systems. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Binding on all adjudicators nationwide (SSR) or per circuit (AR); POMS sections are the day-to-day executable-in-practice rule text; ratifier: Commissioner / Office of General Counsel.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Opposite pattern: historical SSA 'nonacquiescence' - refusing to apply adverse circuit precedent beyond the named claimant to preserve national uniformity; ARs were the 1985-1990s compromise. RECALLED.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Illustrates an institutional reason to refuse precedential effect: uniform national administration outweighs case-by-case consistency with courts.

workflows.economic_pain: Not sourced (backlogs and wait times are publicly reported by SSA OIG; blocked).
workflows.existing_solutions: POMS/HALLEX manuals; DDS case processing systems; SSA's own electronic claims analysis tools. Settlements (rulings) are versioned published prose; POMS is structured manual text, not executable rules.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Government owner; no third-party software buyer for the loop itself.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Rulings are binding by regulation; ALJ decisions are not precedential; APA/Federal Register publication for SSRs/ARs.
workflows.notes: Loop is real and binding but the trigger is courts/policy staff, not front-line escalation; volume of rules is 10^0-10^1 per year against 10^5-10^6 decisions. Nothing verified this session.

workflows.name: VA Office of General Counsel precedent opinions (VAOPGCPREC) vs non-precedential Board of Veterans' Appeals decisions
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED (va.gov blocked). Recalled: BVA decides roughly 10^5 appeals per year; GC precedent opinions in recent years number in the low single digits per year (numbering e.g. VAOPGCPREC 1-2017). Unverified; verify at https://www.va.gov/ogc/opinions.asp.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (recalled structure of compensation claims): A missing evidence ~40%, B factual/medical classification ~30%, C ~15%, E ~5%, H ~5%, D ~5%. Analytical.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: 38 U.S.C. 7104(c) / 38 CFR 14.507: GC precedent opinions bind VA officials including the Board; 38 CFR 20.1303: Board decisions are non-precedential ('binding only with regard to the specific case decided'). The Board Chairman or Under Secretary can request a precedent opinion on a recurring legal question, which then binds prospectively. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Prose opinion binding on all adjudicators; incorporated into the M21-1 adjudication manual; ratifier: VA General Counsel.

workflows.existing_solutions: M21-1 manual, VBMS case system, Board's own decision database (non-precedential, searchable).
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Statutory non-precedential status of individual decisions; precedent only via GC.
workflows.notes: Textbook example of an institution deliberately keeping individual settlements non-precedential and routing generalisation through a separate, low-volume organ.

workflows.name: USCIS: AAO non-precedent decisions -> adopted decisions / precedent decisions / Policy Manual updates
workflows.decision_volume: SOURCED (secondary): a practitioner guide analysed '3,866+ AAO decisions' for EB-1A/NIW alone and reports NIW approval rates dropping 'from 96% to 54%' in 2025-2026 (github.com/HorizonGreen/EB1A-NIW-Guidance; practitioner source, methodology not stated). Adopted decisions per year and Policy Manual update counts NOT SOURCED (uscis.gov blocked); recalled: adopted decisions ~1-3 per year; Policy Manual alerts dozens per year.
workflows.human_review_rate: 100% adjudicator-decided; AAO appeal is a second human review.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: AAO decision content as described by the practitioner guide, which emphasises evidence sufficiency and 'final merits' judgement): A missing evidence ~35%, B factual classification ~20%, E discretion (final merits) ~20%, C ~15%, H ~10%. Analytical.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Applicants mine thousands of non-precedent AAO decisions to infer 'what the immigration bureau is really examining' - de facto precedent use of formally non-precedential decisions.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Informal pattern-mining by applicants; USCIS itself is not bound.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Adopted decisions (designated by the USCIS Director) and BIA/AG precedent decisions bind USCIS adjudicators; Policy Manual updates (policy alerts) codify positions. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Prose guidance binding on adjudicators; ratifier: USCIS Director / Office of Policy & Strategy; lag months to years.

workflows.existing_solutions: USCIS ELIS/CLAIMS case systems; Policy Manual (versioned prose, public); AAO decision reading room.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Government owner; immigration law firms buy research tools (not the loop).
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Non-precedent decisions explicitly not binding; precedent designation reserved to Director/AG.
workflows.notes: Same design as VA/IRS: individual settlements non-precedential; generalisation via a slow, low-volume organ.

workflows.name: Securities/bank regulator staff letters: SEC no-action letters, CFTC/FINRA interpretive letters, OCC interpretive letters, CFPB advisory opinions
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED (sec.gov, occ.gov, cftc.gov, finra.org, fincen.gov blocked). Recalled order of magnitude: SEC Corporation Finance shareholder-proposal no-action requests ~2-3 x10^2 per season; OCC interpretive letters ~10 per year (numbering around 1180-1190 in 2023-2025). Unverified.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: the letters' function as described in publedge PRIOR-ART): C rule interpretation ~60%, G novel structures ~20%, H recurring questions ~15% (evidenced by SEC Staff Legal Bulletins codifying recurring no-action positions - recalled), F ~5%. Analytical.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: SEC no-action letters: 'Explicit reliance language: third parties similarly situated may rely on the position'; 'Clear scope limitation: the letter binds only on the facts presented'; withdrawals/modifications are 'narrative, not structural'; publication is HTML/PDF 'searchable by humans, opaque to agents'. CFPB advisory opinions are published in the Federal Register with versioned numbering; CFTC/FINRA letters follow the same shape.
settlement_loop_evidence.source_type: vendor/open-source prior-art survey (secondary; sec.gov not fetched)
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Similarly-situated third parties may rely on SEC staff positions (a rare explicitly prospective individual settlement); recurring positions are periodically consolidated into Staff Legal Bulletins and rule amendments (RECALLED: e.g., SLB 14 series on shareholder proposals).

workflows.economic_pain: Not sourced (law-firm fees per request are the main cost; unquantified).
workflows.existing_solutions: Agency web archives; Westlaw/Lexis/Bloomberg indexing; law-firm internal no-action databases. Captured as numbered prose letters with narrative supersession; not executable.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Law firms and compliance departments buy research tools; the loop itself is agency-owned.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Staff positions do not bind the Commission; fact-specific; can be withdrawn.
workflows.notes: SEC no-action letters are the one public mechanism where an individual settlement is explicitly reusable by third parties on identical facts - yet the register is still unstructured prose and consolidation into bulletins is slow.

workflows.name: Accounting interpretation: FASB Technical Inquiry Service, IFRS Interpretations Committee agenda decisions, Big-4 national-office consultation databases (PCAOB QC 1000 / ISQM 1)
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED (fasb.org, ifrs.org, iasplus.com, pcaobus.org, viewpoint.pwc.com blocked). Recalled: IFRS IC publishes on the order of 10-20 agenda decisions per year from a few dozen submissions; FASB TIS volume unpublished; Big-4 consultation volumes are internal and unpublished. Unverified.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: the nature of accounting consultations - application of principles-based standards to transactions): C ~50%, H ~25% (firms explicitly maintain consultation precedent databases because questions recur), G ~15%, D ~10% (conflicts between standards/regulators). Analytical.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: IFRS IC agenda decisions are formally non-authoritative explanatory material, but the IASB Due Process Handbook (2020) states entities are expected to implement changes arising from them with 'sufficient time', and securities regulators enforce them. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Published prose; consumed by preparers/auditors; ratified by the Committee with IASB oversight.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: PCAOB QC 1000 (adopted 2024, effective 15 Dec 2025) and IAASB ISQM 1 require firms to consult on difficult or contentious matters, document consultations, and implement the conclusions; Big-4 firms operate national-office consultation databases that function as internal precedent registers. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Internal: documented consultation conclusions are reused by engagement teams and folded into firm methodology manuals (prose); machine-consumption absent.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: FASB Technical Inquiry Service: staff responses are informal, not authoritative, and not published. RECALLED.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Not reusable by others by design.

workflows.existing_solutions: Firm knowledge platforms (Deloitte Technical Library, PwC Viewpoint, KPMG DPP resources - recalled), Workiva/Wdesk for disclosure; consultation logs in audit-methodology tools. Settlements are versioned prose memos, not executable.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: Big-4/next-10 national offices (build in-house); corporate controllers (technical accounting memos).
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Consultation documentation is inspected by PCAOB; privilege/liability concerns keep conclusions internal.
workflows.notes: Structurally the best private analogue of the settlement loop (recurring interpretive questions, an authoritative owner, mandatory documentation, reuse), but entirely unverified this session and already served by in-house firm systems (H3).

workflows.decision_volume: NOT FOUND (lmalloyds.com, content.naic.org blocked; no GitHub artefacts).

settlement_loop_evidence.description: No sourced evidence obtained. Mechanism recalled: LMA issues market claims bulletins; insurers hold internal coverage position papers and claims manuals; coverage counsel opinions. Whether these are versioned and applied prospectively could not be established.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Unknown.

workflows.name: Construction RFIs -> Architect's Supplemental Instructions (AIA G710) -> revised drawings
workflows.decision_volume: NOT SOURCED (aia.org, procore.com, guidehouse.com blocked). Recalled from the Navigant Construction Forum 2013 study: ~796 RFIs per project on average, ~9.9 RFIs per $1M of contract value, ~$1,080 cost per RFI, ~9.7 days median response. Unverified.
workflows.why_humans_review: Estimate (basis: RFI causes commonly reported - unclear/conflicting documents, site conditions, substitutions): C interpretation of drawings/specs ~35%, D conflicts between drawings/specs ~25%, A missing information ~20%, G site-specific ~15%, H ~5%. Analytical.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: An RFI answer that changes the work without cost/time impact is issued as an ASI (AIA G710) and incorporated into the drawing set - prospective for that project only. RECALLED; not fetched.
settlement_loop_evidence.reusable_how: Project-local: later trades follow the revised documents; no cross-project reuse; ratifier: architect of record.

workflows.economic_pain: Recalled ~$1,080 per RFI and schedule delay (unverified).
workflows.existing_solutions: Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Oracle Aconex track RFIs/ASIs as versioned documents (recalled). Settlements are versioned drawings/prose, project-scoped.
workflows.buyer_and_budget: GC/owner project controls; already served by construction management platforms.
workflows.regulatory_constraints: Contractual (AIA A201) rather than regulatory; design liability keeps answers project-specific.
workflows.notes: High volume of interpretive questions but settlements do not generalise beyond the project (G-dominant for the product's purposes) and incumbents already version them.

workflows.name: Meta Oversight Board decisions and policy recommendations -> Community Standards changes
workflows.decision_volume: SOURCED: 147 Board decisions 2020-2025 (Chala 2026, Journal of Online Trust and Safety 3(3), doi:10.54501/jots.v3i3.333, data at github.com/Endalk-Chala/Oversight-Board-Case-Analysis); the enriched CSV holds 128 decisions (2021: 21, 2022: 12, 2023: 42, 2024: 43, 2025: 10), 101 'Overturned' vs 26 'Upheld', 44 summary decisions; top categories Dangerous Individuals and Organizations 26, Hate Speech 9, Violence and Incitement 8. 'Meta should' appears 434 times (mean 3.39 per decision; 53 decisions with none). 40 decisions mention 'parallel context'. Board appeal intake (recalled: ~10^6 user appeals per year) not verified.
workflows.human_review_rate: Board decides ~10^1-10^2 cases per year out of ~10^6 appeals (appeal count recalled). Meta's own review rates not sourced.
workflows.why_humans_review: For Board cases (basis: decision bodies): C policy interpretation ~40%, D conflict between policies/values ~20%, E true discretion (proportionality, newsworthiness) ~25%, H ~15% (recommendations to rewrite policy). Analytical from the corpus sample.

settlement_loop_evidence.description: Meta's tracked responses to 87 Board recommendations (2021-2022 snapshot scraped from oversightboard.com): Implementing fully 27, Implementing in part 21, Assessing feasibility 19, Work Meta already does 14, No further action 6. Example recommendation: 'Meta should rewrite Meta's value of safety to reflect that online speech may pose risk to the physical security of persons and the right to life' (2021-014-IG-UA-1, status Implementing).

evidence_against_thesis: Explicit non-precedent design is the norm for individual settlements across every public mechanism examined: IRS PLRs carry 'Section 6110(k)(3) provides that it may not be used or cited as precedent' (primary, PLR 202301001/003/004 via github.com/surabhitri/PLR_Classification); SEC no-action letters bind 'only on the facts presented' (publedge PRIOR-ART); BVA decisions, AAO non-precedent decisions, FtT decisions and Board case decisions ('identical content with parallel context', 40/128 decision texts) are all deliberately narrow. Generalisation is reserved to a separate, slower organ (Rev. Proc., GC precedent opinion, adopted decision, SSR, ADM memo, classification regulation) at 1-3 orders of magnitude lower volume than case decisions.

In the one production ruling system whose source code was inspected (HMRC ATaR, github.com/hmrc/binding-tariff-classification), the only coded referral reasons are REQUEST_SAMPLE and REQUEST_MORE_INFO: escalation is about missing evidence (category A), supporting H1. Interpretation is done by the same officer and recorded as prose 'justification'.
DWP's own PIP decision tooling investment (github.com/dwp/pip-pre-decision-checks) is in data/evidence completeness checks (CIS data, lay conditions, payability), not in an interpretation register.

Where settlements are already executable and versioned (Kyverno PolicyException registers, github.com/nirmata/demo-gitops-exceptions), the organisation explicitly does not convert recurring exceptions into policy: 'expired exceptions trigger renewal pull requests'; users 'must file fresh requests'. The typed, dated, attributable, revocable grant ledger exists as a feature of the policy engine (supports H3/H6).

PubLedge, an open-source typed/versioned register for exactly this artefact class, attracted 0 stars and no adopters and parked 'standalone product expansion ... pending a concrete legal-graph or adopter demand signal' (github.com/snapsynapse/publedge, INTENT.md decision history 2026-06-09). Direct negative demand signal for a standalone interpretation-register product, at least when aimed at regulators.

Meta implemented only 27 of 87 Oversight Board recommendations fully (21 in part, 19 'assessing feasibility', 14 'work Meta already does', 6 'no further action'; github.com/ryantreves/meta-oversight): even a well-funded, purpose-built settlement-to-policy loop converts about a third of settlements into rules, slowly and non-bindingly.

GitHub's public policy repository explicitly excludes individual cases from the policy-clarification channel ('Please don't post legal complaints') - the case-to-clarification link is not wired even where policy versioning is trivial (github.com/github/site-policy).

IRS PLR volume in the corpus fell from ~1,700/yr (2001-02) to ~550-800/yr (2018-23) as the user fee reached $38,000: institutions ration individual settlements by price and absorb recurring classes into published procedures, shrinking the pool of paid settlements over time rather than compounding it.

Organisational reasons interpretations stay unwritten or non-precedential (analytical, drawn from the mechanisms above; not independently sourced this session): avoiding estoppel/liability (6110(k)(3), 'facts as represented' caveats), preserving discretion and flexibility ('each case on its own merits'), national uniformity versus circuit-by-circuit binding (SSA nonacquiescence/ARs), litigation discovery exposure for insurers' coverage positions, and design/professional liability keeping construction RFI answers project-specific.

No WebSearch was possible (session budget 200/200 already consumed before this task) and every non-GitHub host was blocked, so volumes for rescrit, EBTI, SSR/AR, VA GC, OCC, IFRS IC, ASME, ADM memos and Upper Tribunal could not be verified; absence of these numbers is uncertainty, not support.

found.domain_assessment:
Method caveat first: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this task began, and the egress proxy blocked every government, regulator, court, standards-body, academic and vendor host I tried (about 95 URLs); only github.com and api.github.com (rate-limited) were reachable. Evidence therefore comes from GitHub-hosted primary artefacts (HMRC's production ruling system source, a 28k-document IRS PLR corpus, Oversight Board datasets, PubLedge, Nirmata's exception register, GitHub's policy repo, DWP prototypes) plus explicitly-labelled recalled knowledge for mechanisms I could not fetch. Numbers marked RECALLED are unverified and should be checked at the listed URLs.

Where the loop is real and operational: (1) EU/UK customs rulings. HMRC's ATaR system is a genuine settlement register: every ruling is a structured, dated, versioned Decision (commodity code, effective dates, justification, goods description, search method, exclusion method), cases carry a manager-approved keyword vocabulary, an event log, an appeal ladder and SLA clocks, and completed rulings are published to a public search within a day so later applicants and officers decide against them; divergences escalate to EU classification regulations (recalled). (2) Policy-as-code exception registers (Kyverno PolicyException via PR): the settlement is executable, attributable, dated, expiring and revocable - the 'typed dated grant ledger' the prior investigation thought unshipped exists here as a feature of the policy engine. (3) SSA rulings/POMS, IFRS IC agenda decisions, Coding Clinic, EBA Q&A (all recalled): binding or quasi-binding published interpretation registers, some machine-consumed downstream.

Where the loop is real but slow, prose-only and low-volume: IRS PLR -> revenue procedure (fee $38,000; ~550-800 PLRs/yr in the corpus, down from ~1,700 in 2001; recurring subjects absorbed into checklists/automatic procedures over years), rescrit -> BOFiP RES series, VA GC precedent opinions, USCIS adopted decisions, SEC staff bulletins, UT -> DWP ADM memos. In every one of these the individual settlement is by design non-precedential (6110(k)(3) quoted verbatim; 'facts as represented'; 'identical content with parallel context') and generalisation is a separate governance act by a different organ at 1-3 orders of magnitude lower volume.

Where it is ceremonial or absent: Meta Oversight Board at case level (binding only for identical content; 27 of 87 recommendations implemented fully); GitHub site-policy (cases explicitly excluded from the clarification channel); construction RFI->ASI (project-local); insurer claims bulletins (not found).

Category split across the cluster (analytical): front-line escalation in the only inspected production system is coded as missing evidence (REQUEST_SAMPLE/REQUEST_MORE_INFO), and DWP's tooling investment is in evidence checks - supporting H1 for operational workflows. H (repeatable ambiguity settled prospectively) is clearly present but is handled by institutions as a rule-making function, not a case-handling function, and they ration it deliberately (fees, non-precedent clauses, expiry-and-renew).

Demand signals against a standalone product: PubLedge, an open-source typed/versioned interpretation register covering PLRs, no-action letters, advisory opinions and sandbox agreements, found no adopters and parked its product ambitions in June 2026; Nirmata's register explicitly refuses to turn recurring exceptions into policy; GitHub keeps cases out of policy edits. The strongest Sophon-shaped evidence in this cluster is the private analogue - Big-4 national-office consultation databases and importer classification databases inside GTM suites - both unverified this session and both already built in-house or by incumbents (H3/H6).

Conclusion for this cluster: the settlement loop is a real, named, operational institution mainly where the settled object is a classification that maps to a code (tariff, ICD, commodity) or an executable policy exception; it is ceremonial or deliberately severed wherever the settled object is an interpretation of text. Candidate follow-ups with cheap access to real cases: HMRC/EU customs classification (open-source system, public rulings), AHA Coding Clinic + encoder vendors, and Kyverno/OPA exception registers in large platform teams. I would not pursue regulator-facing interpretation registers (PubLedge signal) or content-policy loops (Oversight Board data).

It is a vendor demo fleet, not an organisation's register, so nothing about recurrence, renewal frequency or refusal to generalise can be inferred from it. The 'one workload' limit is a property of the demo's GitHub issue-form template ('matchConditions are rendered from a fixed template'), not of Kyverno: Kyverno's native PolicyException spec uses an unrestricted MatchResources clause ('Match defines match clause used to check if a resource applies to the exception', https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kyverno/kyverno/main/api/kyverno/v2/policy_exception_types.go), which can match whole namespaces or kinds. Evidence quality should be 'weak' (vendor demo, n=3), and the 'refuses to generalise' finding is a design choice of a demo author, not observed organisational practice.

manual_review_conflated_with_repeatable_: IRS PLRs: the finder assigns H ~15% on the basis that the IRS issues 'guidelines for requests on recurring subjects'. But those recurring-subject checklists are precisely the IRS's already-completed generalisation: taxpayers still pay $38,000 for an individual ruling on a settled class because the law or their auditors require the comfort, which is category H4 (humans stay in the loop after precedent exists), not H. The honest H share for PLRs as a Sophon target is well under 10%: anything genuinely repeatable is either no-ruled as factual, moved to an automatic procedure, or still ruled individually for reasons a register would not remove.

HMRC ATaR / EU BTI: the finder's 'H ~10%' plus 'promising' verdict conflates two things: (a) tariff classification does have a real, structured, prospective settlement loop, and (b) that loop is already implemented by the authority (public ruling search refreshed daily, methodSearch field, keyword governance, classification regulations). Under the brief's section 2 penalties ('existing ... systems already solve the problem adequately', 'implementation requires replacing a core system of record', 'buyer is unclear') the addressable H share for a third-party product is close to zero even if the underlying H share of decisions is 10-20%. This is H3/H6 evidence, not a wedge.

Oversight Board: case-level H is ~0 by design ('identical content with parallel context' clause in 40 of 128 decisions); the finder's 'H ~15% (recommendations to rewrite policy)' is about policy recommendations, which are a rule-making channel (87 in ~20 months, self-reported implementation), not operational case review. Nothing here is a repeated operational decision resolved faster because of a captured settlement.

Kyverno/Nirmata: the finder's 'H ~15% (the same policy gets excepted repeatedly, but the register renews rather than generalises)' is an inference from a demo with three exception manifests. No recurrence data exists. The correct H estimate is 'unknown', and the observed design (expiry-and-renew, fresh justification each time) is the organisation choosing G/E treatment deliberately.

SSA, VA, USCIS, DWP/UT, SEC, IFRS IC, ASME/EBA: every A-H split for these is labelled 'analytical' by the finder and nothing was verified this session either. They should be reported as 'unknown' rather than as percentages; the only defensible structural statement is that each institution routes generalisation through a separate low-volume organ (SSR/AR, GC precedent opinion, adopted decision, ADM memo, Staff Legal Bulletin, agenda decision) at 1-3 orders of magnitude below case volume, which is consistent with H2 (ambiguity that recurs is rare relative to case flow) and H4.

General: across the cluster the finder treats 'the institution has a published-interpretation register' as evidence that H is present. The registers show that H exists at the rule-making layer and is already captured (H3); they say nothing about how much front-line review is repeatable ambiguity versus missing facts, because none of the fetched artefacts records review reasons at case level except HMRC's referral enum (which is evidence-request only).

verification.overall: The finder's GitHub-sourced facts are accurate: every enum, field, count and quotation I re-derived (HMRC ATaR source, the 28,135-file PLR corpus and its year series, the $38,000 fee and '81,000 PLRs' passages, Chala's 128-decision dataset, the 87-recommendation spreadsheet, PubLedge INTENT.md, Nirmata README, GitHub site-policy, DWP prototype views, lex, bofip-mcp) matched verbatim. What does not survive is the weight put on a few of them. The Nirmata 'register' is a three-manifest vendor demo whose one-workload limit is an issue-form template (Kyverno's native PolicyException matches arbitrary resources), so it cannot evidence how organisations govern recurring exceptions. The '27 of 87 implemented fully' figure is Meta's self-reported 30-day commitment from a 2021-22 snapshot. PubLedge's zero adoption is an unmarketed side project, near-zero information about demand. The USCIS '3,866 decisions / 96% to 54%' number has no methodology and should be dropped. The SEC/CFPB reliance language rests on a survey with no primary citations. Beyond that, not one operational volume in the cluster could be verified: WebSearch was exhausted before the task and roughly 50 non-GitHub hosts were policy-denied, so absence of numbers is uncertainty. On the H question: the registers the finder found (Rev. Procs, BOFiP RES, published tariff rulings, SSRs, GC opinions, adopted decisions, ADM memos, IFRS IC agenda decisions) show that repeatable ambiguity is real but is handled as a low-volume rule-making function by a separate organ, and is already captured by the institution (H3), with individual settlements deliberately non-precedential (H4) and generalisation at 1-3 orders of magnitude below case flow (H2). The one production system inspected records escalation as evidence requests, not interpretation, but records a vocabulary, not a rate. Corrected cluster verdict: no workflow here is 'promising' as a standalone Sophon wedge; EU/UK tariff rulings are downgraded to 'uncertain' because the settlement store is already built and public by the authority itself, which makes them the best available source of real historical settlement records for the owner's base-rate experiment while simultaneously being evidence that incumbents (the authority, GTM suites) already own the loop. The strongest evidence in this cluster for a Sophon-shaped market is the existence of structured, dated, published, searched-before-deciding tariff rulings, because it proves the artefact class can be made executable at scale; the strongest evidence against is that every institution examined built that loop itself and kept the individual settlement non-precedential on purpose.
